Description: Private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1861, world-renowned for science, engineering, and technology.
About: MIT's mission is to advance knowledge and educate students in science, technology, and other areas of scholarship that will best serve the world. It is organized around five Schools plus the Schwarzman College of Computing and is known for a hands-on, problem-solving culture ('mens et manus').
Research: Artificial intelligence and computing (CSAIL), robotics, energy and climate, biotechnology and life sciences, materials science, aerospace, nuclear science, economics, and the Media Lab for digital technology and design.
Programs: Engineering, Science, Architecture and Planning, Humanities Arts and Social Sciences, Sloan School of Management, Computing (Schwarzman College of Computing)

Description: Private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1636, the oldest institution of higher education in the US.
About: Harvard is a global leader in liberal arts education and research, comprising Harvard College and twelve graduate and professional schools. Its mission emphasizes educating citizens and citizen-leaders through transformative teaching and research.
Research: Medicine and public health, law, business and economics, government and policy, life sciences, engineering and applied sciences, humanities, and data science.
Programs: Arts and Sciences, Business (HBS), Law, Medicine, Public Health, Education, Engineering and Applied Sciences (SEAS), Design, Divinity, Government (Kennedy School), Dental Medicine, Extension School

Description: Private research university in Stanford, California, founded in 1885, closely tied to Silicon Valley innovation.
About: Stanford's mission is to educate future leaders and promote interdisciplinary teaching and research across the humanities, sciences, engineering, and professional fields, with a strong culture of entrepreneurship.
Research: Artificial intelligence (HAI), computer science, bioengineering, medicine, energy and sustainability (Doerr School), business innovation, and law and policy.
Programs: Engineering, Humanities and Sciences, Business (GSB), Law, Medicine, Education, Earth Sustainability and Energy (Doerr School)

Description: Private Ivy League research university in New York City, founded in 1754, one of the oldest institutions of higher education in the US.
About: Columbia combines a core liberal arts curriculum with extensive graduate and professional education, leveraging its New York City location for global engagement in journalism, business, law, and international affairs.
Research: Climate and earth science (Lamont-Doherty), journalism, international and public affairs (SIPA), biomedical research, data science, and nanoscience.
Programs: Columbia College, Engineering and Applied Science (SEAS), Business, Law, Medicine (Vagelos), Journalism, International and Public Affairs (SIPA), Social Work, Arts, Nursing, General Studies

Description: Private Ivy League research university in Princeton, New Jersey, founded in 1746, known for undergraduate teaching and research.
About: Princeton emphasizes undergraduate liberal arts education alongside graduate research, with no medical, law, or business school, and a strong tradition of independent senior thesis work.
Research: Physics and astrophysics (Plasma Physics Lab), public policy (Woodrow Wilson School/SPIA), economics, computer science, molecular biology, and engineering.
Programs: Engineering and Applied Science, Public and International Affairs (SPIA), Arts and Sciences (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences), Architecture

Description: Private Ivy League land-grant research university in Ithaca, New York, founded in 1865.
About: Cornell is known for its 'any person, any study' philosophy, combining private Ivy League colleges with statutory (land-grant) colleges, and operating a New York City campus (Cornell Tech) and a medical college.

Programs: Agriculture and Life Sciences, Arts and Sciences, Architecture Art and Planning, Business, Engineering, Human Ecology, Industrial and Labor Relations, Hotel Administration, Veterinary Medicine, Computing and Information Science, Cornell Tech, Medicine

Description: Private Ivy League research university in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 1701.
About: Yale is organized around Yale College's liberal arts curriculum and a wide array of graduate and professional schools, with a strong emphasis on the arts, humanities, and residential college life.
Research: Humanities and law, medicine and public health, environmental studies, art and architecture, and molecular and cellular biology.
Programs: Yale College, Law, Medicine, Management (SOM), Art, Architecture, Drama, Divinity, Forestry and Environmental Studies, Music, Nursing, Public Health, Engineering and Applied Science

Programs: The College, Booth School of Business, Law, Medicine (Pritzker), Harris School of Public Policy, Divinity, Social Service Administration (Crown), Molecular Engineering, Physical Sciences, Social Sciences, Humanities

Description: Private research university in Baltimore, Maryland, founded in 1876, recognized as the first US research university.

Description: Private Ivy League research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, founded in 1740 by Benjamin Franklin.
